description: The Grove of Fetters refers to the sacred grove of the Semnones, a Germanic people described by Tacitus in the 1st century AD. According to his Germania, worshippers entered the grove bound with a cord or chain, symbolically acknowledging their submission to the deity believed to rule there, and anyone who fell was required to crawl rather than stand upright. The grove was regarded as an ancient and especially holy center of the Semnones and their wider tribal confederation, illustrating the importance of sacred natural places, ritual submission, communal sacrifice, and tribal identity in early Germanic religion.
